compareDisposition.rationale: The curator examined Hail falls on Egypt beside Pharaoh increases the labor; The promise is repeated to Israel; Moses and Aaron are located in their families; The staff sign is given before Pharaoh. Those passages share its exodus evidence group or Scripture movement, but none supplies a distinct two-source relationship stronger than the accepted comparisons already carrying this topic.

context.body: Flax and barley are struck, while wheat and spelt are not struck because they have not grown up.
context.label: What survives the storm

observations.body: The warning tells Pharaoh to bring servants and livestock from the field into shelter before the hail.
observations.label: Shelter is offered

observations.body: Some servants fear the LORD’s word and bring people and livestock inside; others leave them in the field.
observations.label: Servants divide

observations.body: The hail strikes fields across Egypt, but the passage says there is no hail in Goshen where Israel is.
observations.label: Goshen is distinct

observations.body: Pharaoh confesses, asks for prayer, and promises release; Moses prays and the storm ceases.
observations.label: Confession and relief

observations.body: After seeing the storm stop, Pharaoh sins again, hardens his heart, and does not let Israel go.
observations.label: Refusal returns

payload.posture: Separate the warning, the servants’ different responses, the storm, Pharaoh’s confession, relief, and renewed refusal.
payload.tension: Pharaoh’s confession and promise are followed by renewed sin and refusal once the hail, rain, and thunder cease.
payload.title: A warning divides its hearers
